transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Um… I guess mostly I’m just really tired. I don’t want to make it sound dramatic, but it’s gotten hard to get through a shift at work. My body feels kind of… heavy, like it’s filled with wet sand or something, and even when I rest, I don’t really feel like I come back from it. Does that make sense?
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?

Yeah… I think so. I mean, I don’t want to overstate it, but things just feel kind of flat lately. Like cooking for myself, playing guitar, going hiking, even going over to my family’s place—stuff I normally really like—I still try sometimes, but it feels like I’m just going through the motions, like I’m pretending to care. Does that count?
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um… probably about four months, I think. I mean, not every single second or anything, but this low, empty feeling has kind of been hanging around since after that first burst of energy I had at work faded. It just… didn’t really lift after that. Does that sound like what you mean?
Before this low period started, did you have a time when you felt unusually energized or up compared with your normal self?

Yeah… I mean, I guess there was a stretch where I felt really good, like more cheerful than usual and kind of unstoppable, if that makes sense. At first it seemed like a positive thing, honestly. But I also got… a little more touchy than I want to admit. Like if someone asked me to count a drawer again at work, I’d snap at them harder than the situation really deserved. I’m not proud of that, but yeah, it was different for me.
About how many days in a row did that unusually energized period last?

Um… I think it was around a month, if I’m counting right. It started when the store changed our hours during the remodel. I don’t know if that’s longer than you mean, but yeah, about a month in a row.
During that month when you felt unusually energized, did you need less sleep than usual?

Yeah… I guess I did. I didn’t really think of it as a problem at the time, because with the shift changes it kind of made sense, but I’d sleep maybe just a few hours and still feel really wired, like I didn’t need more. And now it’s more like even when I’m tired, I wake up early and my mind’s already going. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
During that month when you felt unusually energized, did you feel more confident or important than usual?

Um… I don’t know. I mean, I felt better about myself than I usually do, maybe, but I wouldn’t say I thought I was important or anything like that. More like I was just having a good stretch and felt capable. If that makes sense?
During that month when you felt unusually energized, were you more active than usual or taking on a lot more projects?

Yeah… I mean, I was definitely doing more. At work I volunteered to help with extra cash-office stuff, and I started reorganizing shelves, which I told myself was just being helpful. I also made this whole promotion binder, like with ideas and plans and everything.

And then even when I got home, I still felt like I should be doing something—looking at things to buy online, moving furniture around, rearranging my apartment. It didn’t feel bad at the time, just… productive, I guess. Does that count as more active?
During that month when you felt unusually energized, were you talking more than usual?

Maybe… yeah. I didn’t think it was that bad, but people at work did tell me to slow down sometimes. I’d be talking about the schedules or inventory, or ideas I had for supervisors, and I guess I was going really fast because I could see they weren’t keeping up.

I wasn’t trying to talk over anyone or anything… I just had a lot I wanted to explain. Does that make sense?
During that month when you felt unusually energized, did you do anything unusually risky or impulsive, like spending much more money than usual?

I don’t think so… not in a big way. I mean, I might’ve bought a few things online because I was in that “I can organize everything” mindset, but I don’t think it was, like, wildly out of control or anything.

I wasn’t doing anything dangerous that I can think of. At least… I don’t think so. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
During that month when you felt unusually energized, did it cause serious problems at work or in your life?

I guess… yeah, it did cause some problems, even though I was trying really hard to make it seem like I had everything under control.

At work I started making mistakes on the register, and I was falling behind on the cash-office tasks. My manager ended up taking me off some responsibilities I’d been hoping would help me get promoted, which was… embarrassing. I kept telling myself it wasn’t that serious, but it kind of was.

And outside of work, I’ve been avoiding my family some. There was also a point where I needed same-day crisis help because I didn’t feel safe handling it by myself. I don’t know if that’s the kind of “serious problems” you mean, but… yeah, I think it affected things.
